title: Cache a Popular Product
description: A product page has many repeated reads and tolerates a short freshness delay. PostgreSQL owns the truth. Which flow is cache-aside?

options.text: Read the cache; on a miss load PostgreSQL and fill the cache.
options.explanation: The application owns the fallback and fill. Writes should commit to the source before invalidating the cached copy.

options.text: Acknowledge every write in memory and flush it later.
options.explanation: That is write-behind. It changes durability and does not describe the cache-aside read path.

options.text: Read PostgreSQL on every request and never reuse a result.
options.explanation: This keeps the source authoritative but does not cache repeated reads or offload them.

options.text: Synchronously update the database and cache on every write.
options.explanation: That describes write-through, with added write latency and a need to handle partial failure.
